name: Timely Filing 5J.1 — One Claim Line Exceeded the TFL Navigator

steps.hint: Click the 'Event Resolution' tab. The Active Edit panel shows PX_5J — 'Service date exceeds provider allowed filing date' flagged as a Hard Edit (red). That is the event you must resolve.
steps.name: Identify the PX_5J hard edit on Event Resolution
steps.description: Open the Event Resolution tab. All edits on the claim are listed; Edit PX_5J ('Service date exceeds provider allowed filing date') is the active Hard Edit, flagged in red. That is the current event you are resolving.
steps.checklistItem: Event Resolution tab opened — PX_5J hard edit identified
steps.completionTriggerNote: Completes as soon as the trainee opens the Event Resolution tab.

steps.hint: Open the 'Provider Info' tab and scroll to the Billing section — the Timely Filing Limit field is here.
steps.name: Open the Provider Information tab
steps.description: Review the timely filing limit for the claim by opening the claim and scrolling to the Provider Information tab. The timely filing reference is located in the Billing section.
steps.completionTriggerNote: Completes when the trainee opens the Provider Information tab.

steps.hint: Click the '?' icon next to 'Timely Filing Limit' in the Billing section — the Timely filing pop-up opens with the Tax ID and State auto-populated.
steps.name: Open the Timely filing pop-up
steps.description: Navigate to the Provider Information tab, then the Billing section, and click the question mark (?) icon next to the Timely Filing Limit field label. The Timely Filing pop-up window will open, with the provider's Tax ID and State fields automatically populated.
steps.completionTriggerNote: Completes when the trainee clicks the '?' icon, which dispatches the open_tf_popup action.

steps.hint: In the Timely filing pop-up, click 'Search'. The filing-criteria rows appear — note State CA, CFT 52, Contract/LOB Commercial, Effective, End date, TFL 222, and read the Exclusion ind. Here Exclusion ind = Yes, so every field must match the claim before the custom TFL applies.
steps.name: Look up TFL criteria and Exclusion indicator
steps.description: In the Timely filing pop-up, click the Search button. A row of filing criteria will appear with the fields State, CFT, Contract/LOB, Par, Effective, End date, C code, TFL, and Plan type. Note the values: State CA, CFT 52, Contract/LOB Commercial, Effective, End date, and TFL 222. Then interpret the Exclusion indicator: if Exclusion ind = No, the provider is not excluded from the 90-day rule and must submit the claim within 90 days from the date of service; if Exclusion ind = Yes, the provider is excluded and a custom timely filing limit may apply, but only if every field in the pop-up matches the corresponding value on the claim. In this scenario, the Exclusion indicator is Yes, so each field must be compared against the claim before applying the custom limit. Also compare the State displayed in the Timely Filing pop-up with the Pricing State by navigating to the Provider Information tab, then the Rendering section. Confirm that the values match. In this scenario, both fields display CA, indicating that the State requirement has been satisfied.
steps.checklistItem: Look up TFL criteria and Exclusion indicator
steps.completionTriggerNote: Completes when the trainee clicks Search inside the Timely filing pop-up, which dispatches the tf_search action and reveals the filing-criteria rows.

steps.hint: Open 'Claim Data' → 'Details'. Claim type is Professional → CFT 52, which matches the pop-up. The claim summary Receipt date (03/20/2026) falls inside the pop-up's Effective–End range — so the custom 222-day TFL applies.
steps.name: Compare claim fields and determine the applicable filing limit
steps.description: Compare the CFT (Claim File Type) value from the Timely Filing pop-up with the claim type by navigating to the Claim Data tab, then the Details sub-tab, and reviewing the claim information. The CFT value must be 52 for a Professional claim and 53 for an Outpatient claim. In this scenario, the claim type is Professional; therefore, the CFT value is 52. The Contract/LOB value is treated as Commercial in this scenario and requires no further validation. Then, note the Receipt Date from the claim summary and compare it to the Effective Date and End Date displayed in the Timely Filing pop-up to verify whether the Receipt Date falls within the applicable date range. Review the Exclusion Ind value and apply the appropriate filing requirement. If Exclusion Ind = Yes and all applicable fields match the corresponding claim values, the provider must submit the claim within the timely filing limit shown in the TFL field. If Exclusion Ind = Yes but any required field does not match, the provider is subject to the 90-day filing requirement. If Exclusion Ind = No, the provider is also subject to the 90-day filing requirement. In this scenario, Exclusion Ind = Yes and all applicable fields match, including the Receipt Date falling within the Effective Date and End Date range. Therefore, the provider must submit the claim within the 222-day timely filing limit shown in the TFL field. Also determine whether the claim is ITS Home by navigating to the Claim Data tab, then the Details sub-tab, and reviewing the Additional Claim Data section. If the claim is identified as ITS Home, follow the alternate SOP steps. If the claim is identified as Non-ITS Home, proceed to the next step. In this scenario, the claim type is Professional, which is classified as Non-ITS Home; therefore, the trainee may proceed to the next step.
steps.checklistItem: Compare claim fields and determine the applicable filing limit
steps.completionTriggerNote: Completes when the trainee opens the Details sub-tab inside Claim Data to read the claim type. The Receipt-date-vs-Effective/End comparison is on trust (the engine has no date primitive).

steps.hint: Open 'Event Resolution' and look in the All Edits section — the PX_PAJ event is present. Check the Claim Header's Frequency next.
steps.name: Check for the PX_PAJ event
steps.description: Determine whether the claim contains a corrected claim event by looking for the PX_PAJ event in the Event Resolution tab. In this scenario, the PX_PAJ event is present, so the next condition (the Frequency value) must also be checked before concluding whether the claim is a corrected claim.
steps.completionTriggerNote: Completes when the trainee opens the Event Resolution tab to look for the PX_PAJ event.

steps.hint: Open 'Claim Header' and check the Frequency field under General Claim Data. It is not 7 — so even with the PX_PAJ event this is not a corrected claim, and the trainee proceeds.
steps.name: Confirm the Frequency value
steps.description: Confirm the Frequency value by navigating to the Claim Header tab, then the General Claim Data section. A claim is considered a corrected claim when a PX_PAJ event is present and the Frequency field is set to 7. When both conditions are met, the alternate SOP for corrected claims must be followed. If either condition is not met, the claim is not considered a corrected claim, and the trainee may proceed with the next step. In this scenario, the Frequency value is not 7. Therefore, the claim is not a corrected claim, and the trainee may proceed with the next step.
steps.completionTriggerNote: Completes when the trainee opens the Claim Header tab to confirm the Frequency value.

steps.hint: Open 'Event Resolution' again and scan the All Edits section for a PX_SUT event — there is none, so the provider is not Sutter and the trainee proceeds.
steps.name: Check for the PX_SUT event
steps.description: Determine whether the provider is Sutter by looking for the PX_SUT event in the Event Resolution tab. If the PX_SUT event is present, follow the Sutter procedure; if it is absent, the provider is not Sutter and the trainee proceeds. In this scenario, the PX_SUT event is absent, so the trainee proceeds.
steps.completionTriggerNote: Completes when the trainee opens the Event Resolution tab again to look for the PX_SUT event.

steps.hint: Open 'Claim Header' again and check the Provider Participation field under General Claim Data. It reads PAR and the claim is Professional — both conditions are met, so the alternate SOP applies and continues with the steps below.
steps.name: Verify claim type and provider participation
steps.description: Verify the claim type and provider status by navigating to the Claim Header tab, then the General Claim Data section, and reviewing the Provider Participation field. For this workflow, the alternate SOP applies only when the claim type is Professional and the provider status is PAR, indicating a participating provider. If both conditions are met, follow the alternate SOP steps. If either condition is not met, proceed to the next step. In this scenario, the claim type is Professional and the provider status is PAR; both conditions are met, so the trainee follows the alternate SOP steps that follow.
steps.checklistItem: Verify claim type and provider participation
steps.completionTriggerNote: Completes when the trainee opens the Claim Header tab again to verify the Provider participation field.

steps.hint: Open 'Claim Lines'. Read each line's From date and the claim summary Receipt date (03/20/2026). One line's From date is more than 222 days earlier — that line is outside the TFL, which raised the PX_5J event, so the trainee proceeds.
steps.name: Calculate filing window against the TFL
steps.description: Open the Claim Lines tab and note the Service from date of each claim line — there are three claim lines in this scenario. From the claim summary, note the Receipt date and calculate the difference between each claim line's Service from date and the Receipt date — three separate calculations, one per claim line. If the difference is within the 222-day TFL that claim line is within the TFL. A claim within the TFL follows the alternate SOP steps; a claim outside the TFL proceeds. In this scenario, one of the three claim lines falls outside the 222-day TFL — which is why the PX_5J event was raised — so the claim is not within the TFL and the trainee proceeds.
steps.checklistItem: Calculate filing window against the TFL
steps.completionTriggerNote: Completes when the trainee opens the Claim Lines tab. The actual TFL math is on trust (the engine has no date primitive).

steps.hint: Open 'Search' → 'Claims', enter the Service to date, and click 'Search'. Two claims appear — open the Resolved-Cancelled claim's member information; the Finalization code PX_RDELEP confirms it was previously deleted.
steps.name: Look up prior deleted claims
steps.description: Review the member's claim history to check whether the same claim was previously deleted due to incorrect data or because the provider data was not loaded in the database at the time. Navigate to the Search tab → Claims sub-tab — the Service from date, HCID, and Provider Tax ID are auto-populated. Enter the Service to date and click Search. If two matching claims are shown — one with status Resolved-Cancelled — open the cancelled claim's member information; if the Finalization code field shows PX_RDELEP, the claim was previously deleted.
steps.completionTriggerNote: Completes when the trainee clicks Search on the Search → Claims sub-tab, which dispatches the claims_search action and reveals the two matching claims.

steps.hint: Click 'View member information' on the Resolved-Cancelled claim, then 'Open Claim Detail' in the dialog. One of its three claim lines is outside the TFL — the deleted claim was outside the TFL, so the trainee proceeds.
steps.name: Verify the deleted claim's filing window
steps.description: Search tab → Claims sub-tab → View member information → Open claim detail. To check whether the deleted claim was within the TFL, click Open Claim Detail. The deleted claim's details appear in the same layout as the current claim. Go to its Claim Lines and note the Service from date of each of its three claim lines, then calculate the difference between each Service from date and the Receipt date. If the deleted claim is within the TFL, follow the alternate SOP steps; if it is outside the TFL, proceed. In this scenario, one of the three claim lines on the deleted claim falls outside the TFL — the same PX_5J condition — so the deleted claim is not within the TFL and the trainee proceeds.
steps.checklistItem: Verify the deleted claim's filing window
steps.completionTriggerNote: Completes when the trainee clicks 'Open Claim Detail' on the Resolved-Cancelled claim, which dispatches the open_prior_claim action. The filing-window calculation is on trust (the engine has no date primitive).

steps.hint: Open 'Attachment' → 'Attachments' and review the PWK section. The Type and Document number fields are populated, but the proof has not been approved — so proceed to reject the claim.
steps.name: Check for Acceptable Proof in PWK section
steps.description: Check whether Acceptable Proof has been received to override the TFL. Navigate to the Attachments tab → Attachments sub-tab and review the PWK section. If a proof document has been submitted, the Type and Document number fields will be populated. If proof has been received and approved, apply the TF bypass code and continue processing; if no proof has been received or it has not been approved, proceed to reject the claim. In this scenario, although the attachment fields are populated with values indicating a submission, the proof has not been approved, so the trainee proceeds to reject the claim.
steps.checklistItem: Check for Acceptable Proof in PWK section
steps.completionTriggerNote: Completes when the trainee opens the Attachments sub-tab on the Attachment tab to review the PWK section.

steps.hint: Open the 'Notes' tab and look at the Task Management section — the BEN field reads SPIDER, so the trainee proceeds.
steps.name: Identify the benefit type
steps.description: Determine the benefit type. Open the Notes tab and navigate to the Task Management section, then check the BEN field to identify the benefit. If the benefit is SPIDER, proceed; if it is Non-Spider, follow the alternate SOP steps. In this scenario, the benefit is SPIDER, so the trainee proceeds.
steps.completionTriggerNote: Completes when the trainee opens the Notes tab to read the BEN field in the Task Management section.

steps.hint: Action menu → Deny Claim. Enter reject code PX_00169 in the Deny Claim section, click Submit, then confirm the pop-up.
steps.name: Deny the claim using Reject code PX_00169
steps.description: Apply reject code PX_00169 as defined in the SOP for this line-level rejection. From the Action menu, select Deny Claim. A new Deny Claim section will appear below the header. Enter reject code PX_00169 in the input box — the matching code will appear in a dropdown list — select it and click Submit.
steps.checklistItem: Deny the claim using Reject code PX_00169
steps.completionTriggerNote: Completes when the trainee submits the Deny Claim panel (which dispatches the deny_claim action).

steps.hint: Click Submit and confirm in the dialog.
steps.name: Submit decision
steps.completionTriggerNote: Completes when the trainee confirms the Deny decision in the submit dialog.

description: Resolve the PX_5J edit (service date exceeds the provider's allowed filing date): open the Timely filing pop-up and review the filing criteria and Exclusion indicator, compare State and CFT against this Professional claim and determine that the custom 222-day TFL applies, confirm the claim is a Non-ITS Home non-corrected claim, walk the Sutter gate, find that the Professional / PAR participation gate puts the claim on the alternate SOP, verify one of three claim lines was filed outside the 222-day window, confirm the prior deleted claim was also outside the TFL, check the PWK section, confirm the benefit is SPIDER, then deny with line-level reject code PX_00169.

stepSummaryForResults.name: Event Resolution tab opened — PX_5J hard edit identified
Frequency not 7 — not a corrected claim
PX_SUT event absent — provider is not Sutter
One claim line outside the 222-day TFL
Deleted claim confirmed outside the TFL
PWK proof submitted but not approved
Deny Claim panel submitted with PX_00169
